summary: A is the better merge candidate because it keeps replayability and multipart construction localized to FilesService and centralizes request handling, while B makes an SDK-wide RawClient behavior change and duplicates Files.Add logic inside Upload.
reasons: A reuses internal/multipartbody.NewFile and verifies the multipart field, filename, content, and complete body replay across a 429 using an os.File source.

A factors the existing request, option, decoding, and error path into a shared add helper, preserving one implementation path. B copies that machinery into Upload, directly conflicting with the contract’s requirement to route through FilesService.Add and increasing divergence risk.

B changes RawClient.Do so nearly every non-native io.Reader across the SDK is eagerly buffered whenever retries are active. This broad change affects memory use and source-read timing for unrelated APIs and violates the contract’s scope restriction against changing unrelated retry machinery.
B has stronger validation and source-reader-error tests, but those test-quality advantages do not outweigh its broader semantic change and duplicated FilesService implementation.
risks_a: Upload calls the private add helper rather than FilesService.Add literally, so it does not exactly follow the required routing contract even though it shares the same implementation.
Add now eagerly reads every caller-provided body, changing its streaming and error-timing behavior despite the instruction to preserve existing behavior.
The patch adds no explicit Upload tests for empty filenames, nil content, or source-reader failures; validation is left to multipartbody.NewFile rather than being visible at the API boundary.
risks_b: Upload duplicates Add’s option handling, request construction, response decoding, and missing-data error instead of routing through Add.
The RawClient change introduces global eager buffering for arbitrary reader bodies, expanding scope and potentially causing large memory allocations in unrelated endpoints.
The documented WithNoRetry-dependent streaming behavior adds a new cross-cutting semantic distinction not requested by the frozen contract.
